AUTHOR: Bonofiglio, F; De Leo, FC; Yee, C; Chatzievangelou, D; Aguzzi, J; Marini, S
TITLE: Machine learning applied to big data from marine cabled observatories: A case study of sablefish monitoring in the NE Pacific
REGION: Barkley Canyon, NEPTUNE observatory (Ocean Networks Canada), NE Pacific
DATA: Own ONC cabled-observatory video, 3 sites (Node 620 m, Axis 985 m, Upper Slope 420 m), Sep 2019-Feb 2020, 9772 clips; 3647 annotated frames
V_EV: Table 1 / Sec 2.1: 'Node, 620 m'; 'a pair of dimmable ROS LED lights (100 W, > 406 lm), which provided illumination during video recording.'
D2: 2917 train / 730 test frames; plus 5-fold CV within training/validation
D_EV: Sec 3.1: '9205 tagged unique sablefish individuals distributed in 3647 image-frames, used for training (n = 2917) and testing (n = 730)'; Table 1 note: 'simple random selection of frames'
R_EV: Sec 2.1-2.2: all training, test and count-validation data come from the same three Barkley Canyon cameras over one 4.5-month period
C_EV: Sec 3.2: 'filtering only detections with the confidence value ... greater or equal than 80% for the Node and Axis sites and 95% for Slope'; higher value 'needed to better discriminate'
E_EV: Sec 3.3: 'For site Node and Axis, we measured 88% and 81% Pearson correlation' between AI count time series and manual MaxN of 30-s clips from the same videos
ARCH: YOLOv5 detector + Euclidean-centroid tracker for counting
METR: AP@0.5, precision, recall, 5-fold CV AP; Pearson correlation of count time series with manual MaxN
NOTE: Train/test split described as frame counts with random frame selection (Table 1 note); no grouping by video stated. Manual MaxN comparison was on clips not used in training but from the same footage/cameras (called 'independent visual counts' by authors, but same imagery -> 같은 영상). Per-site thresholds (0.8 vs 0.95) justified -> C P. Tracking used to reduce multiple counts with sensitivity analysis on parameter m (Fig 8) but no duplicate/FP measurement -> C5 none; verifier may reconsider. Manual confirmation of counts >100 noted without FP rate. Recall 52% explicitly discussed -> E4 FNR.
